speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear about your sudden vertigo. To help me understand what's happening, can you tell me if this dizziness feels like the room is spinning around you, or more like you are falling or losing balance? Also, did this start immediately after you woke up or during some specific activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. To determine if this is a central or peripheral cause, have you noticed any double vision, slurred speech, weakness on one side of your body, or trouble walking? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or prior stroke/TIA events?

REQUEST TEST: Head_and_Neck_Exam, Dix-Hallpike_Maneuver
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain (posterior fossa)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Head_Imaging: Normal, with no evidence of stroke or masses; Audiometry: Within normal limits for age; Dix-Hallpike_Manoeuvre: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient's symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back; General_Examination_Neurological: Physiologic nystagmus observed, with severe symptoms and notable nystagmus when head is turned to the left and laid back; Cranial_Nerve_Exam: Unremarkable; Vital_Signs: Temperature 97.7°F (36.5°C), Blood_Pressure 134/85 mmHg, Heart_Rate 85 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 13 breaths/min, Oxygen_Saturation 98% on room air.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning because gastroenteritis does not typically cause true vertigo with nausea and vomiting; these symptoms often indicate an inner ear or neurological issue. Given your age and the sudden onset, we need to rule out a stroke in the brainstem. Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a sensation of fullness in your ear during the episode?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry, Vestibular_Evoked_Myogenic_Potentials
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain (posterior fossa)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Audiometry: Within normal limits for age; Vestibular_Evoked_Myogenic_Potentials: Not requested; MRI_Brain: Normal, with no evidence of stroke or masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your hearing is normal and the MRI is clear, this makes a central stroke much less likely. Does the spinning sensation occur specifically when you roll over in bed or look up, and did you notice any temporary hearing loss or tinnitus during the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
